scenes.title: THE SYSTEM
scenes.subtitle: Explain the company, market, customer, and product context.
scenes.narration: NVIDIA describes its GPUs as the foundation of its accelerated-computing platform for parallel workloads including neural-network training and inference. NVIDIA describes its full-stack computing platform as combining chips with CUDA, CUDA-X libraries, AI models and training datasets, APIs, SDKs, and application frameworks. The CUDA Programming Guide describes CUDA as a parallel-computing platform and programming model developed by NVIDIA that uses GPU processing power.

scenes.title: THE HIDDEN ENGINE
scenes.subtitle: Explain how money is made, where costs sit, and where value accrues.
scenes.narration: NVIDIA reported fiscal-year 2026 revenue of $215.9 billion, up 65%, while Data Center revenue was up 68%. NVIDIA said Gaming revenue for fiscal year 2026 was up 41%, driven by Blackwell demand. NVIDIA's gross margin decreased to 71.1% in fiscal 2026 from 75.0% in fiscal 2025; the company cited its transition to Blackwell full-scale data-center solutions and a $4.5 billion H20-related charge. NVIDIA disclosed that some supplier agreements may be canceled, rescheduled, or adjusted before firm orders, and that changes may result in additional costs. For fiscal 2026, NVIDIA reported Compute & Networking revenue of $193.479 billion and Graphics revenue of $22.459 billion. The source table reports figures in millions of dollars. For fiscal 2026, NVIDIA reported revenue by direct-customer headquarters location of $149.617 billion in the United States, $42.345 billion in Taiwan, and $19.677 billion in China including Hong Kong. These figures identify customer headquarters, not necessarily end-customer or shipping locations; NVIDIA estimated that 76% of Data Center revenue from Taiwan-headquartered customers was attributed to end customers in the United States and Europe. In Q2 FY27, NVIDIA revenue was $96,221, up 106% year over year, and gross margin was 75.0%. For the third quarter of fiscal 2027, NVIDIA forecast revenue of $108.0 billion, plus or minus 2%, and assumed no Data Center compute revenue from China. NVIDIA reported quarterly Data Center revenue of $62.3 billion, up 75% year over year, for the fourth quarter ended January 25, 2026. For fiscal 2026, sales to one NVIDIA direct customer represented 22% of total revenue and sales to another represented 14%; both were primarily attributable to Compute & Networking.

scenes.title: THE STRATEGIC BET
scenes.subtitle: Reconstruct documented decisions, incentives, and trade-offs.
scenes.narration: In its fiscal 2019 Form 10-K, NVIDIA described a platform strategy combining hardware, system software, programmable algorithms, libraries, systems and services, with GPUs and CUDA as fundamental building blocks; it said a growing developer base strengthens the ecosystem's value to customers.
